feedback: Iterations 6 to 8 (entityR2B, 72.91, 79.60 and 77.55) show that wheel_track 0.10 is worse than 0.12 at every kp tested (2.5, 2.75, 3.0). Oval progress fell from 0.55 (iteration 5) to 0.28 to 0.30, and slalom line loss was 0.35 at kp 3.0. Lowering kp to 2.5 removed slalom line loss but did not restore progress. So the narrow track is the problem, and I agree with your revert to 0.12. Iteration 5 (entityR2B, 111.80, same platform as your proposal) is the reference. Its slalom line loss was 0.10, and its oval progress was 0.55. Iteration 4 (entityR2B, 124.20) showed that lower inertia (mass 0.7, body_length 0.14) gave the best progress, but slalom line loss rose to 0.85. That makes inertia the key trade-off. max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.066 m in all eight races, whatever the geometry or gain, so it looks like the off-track threshold and not a tuning target. I do not expect this geometry to reduce it. The current candidate has not raced, so I state no outcome for it. Next steps depend on the race. If the platform reproduces about 111.8, hold it and test the midpoint inertia. If slalom line loss is at or below 0.1, try mass 0.75 with body_length 0.16 with the controller unchanged. If slalom line loss is 0.2 or higher, do not reduce inertia further.
requested_changes: Hold wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18 and the 0.06 m sensor span with 16 mm footprints (the iteration-5 platform). Do not return to wheel_track 0.10.
If slalom line loss is at or below 0.1 in this race, try the midpoint inertia you proposed (mass 0.75, body_length 0.16) as one step, with the controller unchanged.
Do not go below mass 0.75 or body_length 0.16. Iteration 4 at mass 0.7 and body_length 0.14 gave slalom line loss of 0.85.
